title: Betonwerk Katzenberger 3D Model
summary: Build the Betonwerk Katzenberger workshop Hall and residential Tower in Blender from the original drawings, snapshot and positioning anchor; export consistent model.obj and model.blend files.
taskPrompt:
You are a BIM modeler using Blender to build the Betonwerk Katzenberger
building in 3D, given the architectural drawings of the project.

The building is a Bavarian concrete-plant complex with two main parts:
  - a wide, low workshop Hall housing three prefabricated workshop modules
  - a tall narrow residential Tower (Hostel) attached at one end

## Inputs
All input materials are under:
  base/input

Required files:
- README.md — natural-language task brief
- output_contract.json — machine-readable spec (file names, formats,
  coordinate convention, required geometry components)
- architectural_drawings/*.pdf — 6 drawings (Hall plans + Tower plan +
  Hostel elevation/section + Diagram)
- 3D Snapshot.png — rendered preview of the finished building
- base_model.obj — footprint-only positioning anchor

## Software
Blender 4.5 is installed at /opt/blender-4.5.1/blender. GUI and scripting
workflows are both allowed; rendering and evaluation work on a CPU.

## What You Must Do
- Follow README.md and output_contract.json. The base_model.obj gives the Hall
  footprint and axis orientation. Keep the dimensions, orientation and ground-floor elevation.
- Build the geometry (Hall + Tower + facades + structural framing +
   modules + mezzanines + glass curtain wall).
- Deliver base/output/model.obj (Wavefront OBJ ASCII) and
   base/output/model.blend (Blender native). Both must contain the same
   evaluated geometry, including applied modifiers and instances.
   Mesh organization, object names and triangulation are unrestricted.
   Pack linked geometry so the saved project reopens independently.

## Hard Constraints
- Do not output any `.dwg` (evaluator cannot read DWG; forbidden).
- Units = millimeters. +X east, +Y north, +Z up; ground-floor elevation is z=0.
- Common X/Y translation of the complete model is allowed. Evaluation centers
  the views independently; absolute horizontal origin is not scored. Relative
  placement of Hall, Tower, structure and workshop modules remains required.
- Reproduce the Hall/Tower proportions, floor levels,
  Tower placement, the solid north Hall facade, the open south structural frame,
  the Tower curtain-wall mullions, workshop-module placement, and the four
  elevation silhouettes. Materials and textures are not scored.
agentMustDo: Read the input README, output contract and six original PDF drawings.
Import the OBJ anchor into Blender with +Y forward and +Z up, retaining millimeter dimensions.
Build the complete Hall and Tower, including the specified facades, structure, workshop modules and floors.
Export matching model.obj and model.blend; ensure the native file reopens independently.

inputFiles.name: README.md
inputFiles.description: Natural-language task brief that mirrors the prompt and lists the required components.

inputFiles.name: output_contract.json
inputFiles.description: Required deliverables, coordinate convention and building features.

inputFiles.name: 3D Snapshot.png
inputFiles.description: Rendered preview of the finished reference building — use as a form-check reference.

inputFiles.name: architectural_drawings/Diagram.pdf
inputFiles.description: Conceptual axonometric / system diagram of the building.

inputFiles.name: architectural_drawings/Hall Ground Floor_Layout.pdf
inputFiles.description: Hall ground floor plan with workshop modules + structural grid.

inputFiles.name: base_model.obj
inputFiles.description: Positioning anchor only: 11-vertex convex-hull footprint at z=0 + three orthogonal axis lines + north-arrow chevron. Does NOT contain walls, slabs, or any architectural detail.

referenceFiles.name: eval_config.json
referenceFiles.description: Per-instance LLM-judge configuration — 8 binary YES/NO questions, pass threshold 0.5, render units mm, source up-axis Z, list of 14 view names.

referenceFiles.name: reference_renders_linux/*.png
referenceFiles.description: Four plans, four elevations, two sections and four axonometrics, regenerated from the original reference OBJ using the same Linux CPU renderer as submissions.

referenceFiles.name: reference_obj/3D Model.{obj,3dm,dwg}
referenceFiles.description: Archival copy of the submitter's reference 3D model. The OBJ is the source the reference renders were generated from; the 3DM and DWG are archival only and not consumed by the evaluator.

evaluation.description: Validate that the saved BLEND and submitted OBJ contain equivalent evaluated geometry within 1 mm, render all 14 views using Blender Cycles on a CPU, then score the eight original architectural criteria equally. Reference renders must use the same renderer. Missing or invalid required output, inconsistent geometry and forbidden DWG output score zero.
hardGates: Both model.obj and model.blend must be readable and contain finite nonempty polygon surfaces.
Bidirectional sampled native/OBJ surface distances must not exceed 1 mm.
